# pg_procrustes

> A fast, flexible PostgreSQL SQL formatter written in Go. Driven by the native PostgreSQL parser (libpg_query), it understands SQL exactly like the database itself and reformats it according to a declarative YAML configuration.

pg_procrustes reformats PostgreSQL SQL files according to `.pg_procrustes.yaml`. It is idempotent: running it twice produces the same result. It handles plain SQL, DML, DDL, CTEs, and PL/pgSQL function bodies (dollar-quoted blocks). Every option can be set to `preserve`, so the formatter only touches what you ask it to.

For the complete documentation in a single file (README + fully commented reference config), read [llms-full.txt](https://pg_procrustes.80.cz/llms-full.txt).

## Key facts

- Language: Go (CGO, uses libpg_query via pg_query_go)
- License: MIT
- Config file: `.pg_procrustes.yaml` (auto-detected from the current directory upward, or `-c <path>`)
- Platforms: macOS (arm64, amd64), Linux (amd64, arm64), Windows (amd64, arm64)
- Install: `brew install heptau/tap/pg-procrustes`, `go install github.com/heptau/pg_procrustes/cmd/pg_procrustes@latest`, or a binary from GitHub Releases
- Editor integration: Neovim plugin (conform.nvim formatter, `:PgProcrustesFormat`), plus config-only setups for Zed, VS Code, JetBrains/DataGrip, Emacs, Helix, Vim (ALE)

## CLI usage

```
pg_procrustes [flags] [file ...]      # no files → read stdin, write stdout
```

- `-w` — write result back to source files
- `--check` — exit 1 if any file would change (CI / pre-commit)
- `--diff` — print unified diff without writing
- `--backup[=.ext]` — save original before overwriting (requires `-w`)
- `--out-dir <dir>` — write formatted files to a different directory
- `-c <path>` — explicit config file path
- `-v`, `--version` — print version

## What it formats

- Casing of reserved keywords, keywords, data types, literals, operators, schemas, tables, columns, functions, conditional functions (COALESCE, NULLIF, …), system functions (CURRENT_DATE, …), aliases, PL/pgSQL variables and keywords; per-word casing exceptions
- Data type form: long (`character varying`), short (`varchar`), or long without spaces
- Alias `AS`: add / remove; `<>` vs `!=`; `NOT IN` vs `<> ALL`; `CAST(x AS t)` vs `x::t`; explicit/implicit `ASC`; short/long JOIN form; removing `public.` and safe double quotes
- Spacing: operators, commas, parentheses, inline whitespace; trailing whitespace, trailing newline, semicolons, blank lines
- Layout: clause breaking, content breaking (comma lists, AND/OR conditions), CASE expressions, UNION blank lines, paren-indented blocks, indentation
- PL/pgSQL: DECLARE/BEGIN/EXCEPTION/END structure, IF/ELSIF/ELSE, LOOP/FOR/WHILE, CASE statements

## Top-level config keys

`reserved_keywords`, `keywords`, `data_types`, `literals`, `operators`, `schemas`, `tables`, `columns`, `functions`, `conditional_functions`, `system_functions`, `aliases`, `plpgsql_variables`, `plpgsql_keywords`, `trailing_whitespace`, `trailing_newline`, `semicolons`, `inequality_op`, `join_form`, `operator_spacing`, `comma_spacing`, `blank_lines`, `paren_spacing`, `inline_spacing`, `quoted_identifiers`, `schema_qualification`, `cast_style`, `order_asc`, `not_in`, `layout` (`line_length`, `indent`, `clauses`, `content`, `case`, `union`, `dollar_quote`, `paren_indent`).
